dataset.citation: Vassil Panayotov, Guoguo Chen, Daniel Povey, and Sanjeev Khudanpur. LibriSpeech: An ASR Corpus Based on Public Domain Audio Books. ICASSP 2015.
dataset.attribution: LibriSpeech, prepared by Vassil Panayotov with assistance from Daniel Povey; corpus authors Panayotov, Chen, Povey, and Khudanpur (2015). Derived from LibriVox public-domain audiobook recordings. Distributed by OpenSLR under CC BY 4.0; mirrored on Hugging Face. Local adaptation: lossless FLAC decoding to full, untrimmed 16 kHz mono signed 16-bit little-endian PCM. No gain, normalization, denoising or noise was applied.

selection.rule: Use the two initially probed fixed rows, provided both are unused speakers and each is at least four seconds. Selection and references were frozen before any recognition-model call on these clips.
selection.novelty_check: Read existing conformance/corpus/resolution manifests and searched experiments, evidence, conformance, artifacts, docs, tools and infra including ignored files for speaker 260/chapter 123286 and speaker 4446/chapter 2275; no prior matching use was found before acquisition.
selection.heldout_scope: New relative to this project's previous fixtures and model observations, not claimed excluded from Whisper training. Two short clean read-speech clips are a smoke check, not a broad accuracy/generalization study.
selection.reference_origin: Independent LibriSpeech reference text from the selected source rows, not model output.
selection.acquisition_note: Before the final instruction to keep initial clips arrived, a duration-only probe fetched rows 200 through 209 seeking a 10-16-second utterance. All were shorter than ten seconds; it stopped without saving candidates or running models. The final choice returned to the original rows 200 and 1200, not recognition outcomes.
selection.transfer_accounting: Final selected-source transfer is exact. The earlier ten transient FLAC probes were not retained or individually byte-count logged; 10 MiB is a conservative bound, not measured transfer. Including all 12 FLAC requests and 14 metadata requests, conservative total bound is 14,361,583 bytes, below 15 MB.
